entry.evidence: its genesis and geomorphic stability have not been well understood

sequences.source_document: Nanson et al. 2022, Marine Geology 445, 106731 (published PDF and XML text)

steps.action: Posed the problem that the genesis and stability of the shelf-incising Perth Canyon are not understood, and set the aim of mapping its geomorphology, controls, evolution and recent activity.
steps.quote: its genesis and geomorphic stability have not been well understood

steps.action: Framed rival initiating mechanisms (mass wasting versus turbidity-current erosion) and three rival turbidity-current triggers: failed sediment, river discharge from the palaeo-Swan River, and resuspended shelf-edge sediment.
steps.quote: we consider morphologic, geomorphic and geologic evidence for their primary initiating mechanisms

steps.action: Took up the hypothesis from early studies that a Swan River connection drove the canyon's origin or headward extension.
steps.quote: The connection between the Perth Canyon and the Swan River has been invoked as a possible mechanism for the headward extension

steps.action: Designed the test of the Swan River connection: legacy seismic reflection profiles analysed with Vlaming well data and canyon dredge samples.
steps.quote: To test this connection, we explore links to the deeper subsurface by analysing seismic reflection profiles intersecting the Perth Canyon

steps.action: Assembled and processed multibeam bathymetry (20 m, 40 m and 250 m grids), backscatter (CMST-GA toolbox), MARS sediment samples, a piston core, sub-bottom insights and 1970s–2000s legacy seismic surveys.
steps.quote: We have assembled data on the Perth Canyon from a range of published documents and repositories

steps.action: Applied the two-part Dove et al. (2020) scheme: a 5° slope classification outside the canyon and a TPI classification (1 km neighbourhood, thresholds chosen by trial and error) inside it, followed by manual editing into IHO-based Morphology features.
steps.quote: we used the topographic position index (TPI) method (Weiss, 2001) to map morphological features as bathymetric highs, lows and intermediate categories

steps.action: Produced the Step 1 Morphology map: Escarpments, Spurs and Gullies, Terraces, Platforms, and Holes alternating with Ridges along the canyon floor and mouth.
steps.quote: Semi-automated mapping of the seabed surrounding Perth Canyon reveals a predominantly low gradient surface

steps.action: Built thalweg long profiles and cross-sections, separated reaches by polynomial breaks in slope, and measured reach gradients, w/t ratios and nick-points, comparing the mouth Holes with those of a blind canyon.
steps.quote: We fitted a 4th order polynomial line of best fit to the profile (unillustrated) to more objectively demarcate these breaks in slope

steps.action: Checked that backscatter reflects sediment character by comparing it with prior sediment-wave and sand-facies interpretations from sub-bottom profiles and with sediment samples.
steps.quote: These consistencies between the backscatter, sub-bottom (Heap et al., 2008) and sediment sample data support the usefulness of these backscatter data

steps.action: Read slab and slump failures over the Valanginian Unconformity, and fault-bounded headwalls, from shallow seismic sections across mapped escarpments.
steps.quote: Seismic sections C-F (Fig. 10) demonstrate clear failure planes and the displacement of relatively intact strata.

steps.action: Stated rival interpretations for the mid-canyon Ridges and Holes: accretionary bedforms versus displaced slumped blocks.
steps.quote: While their morphology and size are also consistent with displaced blocks of slumped material

steps.action: Favoured the accretionary-bedform interpretation from arcuate planform, downstream-reducing crest heights and hydraulic position in a widening, lower-gradient reach.
steps.quote: we favour their interpretation as accretionary features on the basis of their arcuate planform

steps.action: Stated two interpretations for the large canyon-mouth undulations: cyclic steps formed by supercritical turbidity currents, or intact back-tilted blocks of failed strata.
steps.quote: We suggest two possible interpretations for these features.

steps.action: Compared upslope-dipping internal reflectors (Fig. 10G) and the piston core's fining-upward turbidite packages with a surface lag against the cyclic-step expectation, which supported cyclic steps while the block alternative was retained.
steps.quote: support their interpretation as turbidite deposits that comprise the youngest bedsets of large cyclic steps

steps.action: Extrapolated the interpretations of representative units to tag all Morphology polygons with geomorphic classes, producing the Step 2 Geomorphology map.
steps.quote: by extrapolating insights from the detailed geomorphic interpretations of representative units (described above) across the study area

steps.action: Related mass-movement types and canyon alignment to faults, stratigraphy, the Edwards Island Block, the Bathurst Syncline and the Harvey Transfer Zone using seismic sections and the Valanginian palaeo-topography; extended in Discussion 4.1.
steps.quote: Faults control the positions of the head scarps of these failures (Fig. 10D-F)

steps.action: Judged turbidity-current bedforms recently inactive from backscatter (trough draping, winnowed crests) and the core's surface lag.
steps.quote: several of their characteristics suggest that they have been recently inactive

steps.action: Used the 2018 M5.2–5.3 earthquakes as found conditions: differenced the pre-event grid (2014/2015) and the post-event grid (December 2018) over the canyon headwall.
steps.quote: Regionally significant earthquakes in 2018 provided a rare opportunity to examine the likely impacts of such events on canyon headwall stability

steps.action: Found only localised source-to-sink movement from a gully amphitheatre and slump headwalls, and noted that the 4-year window prevents attributing it to the earthquakes alone.
steps.quote: these results indicate that the cumulative effects of all seafloor processes over the period of comparison are limited

steps.action: Identified three stacked infilled palaeovalleys (PV1–PV3) landward of the headwall in legacy seismic line PV91-r-17, with dimensions, w/t ratios and stratigraphic ages.
steps.quote: Seismic data from the Vlaming Sub-Basin, between the modern canyon headwall and coast, reveals several palaeo-incisions (Fig. 14)

steps.action: Compared palaeovalley w/t ratios with a fluvial compilation and with the modern canyon, concluding they are river-cut incised valleys, and matched the PV1 base depth to the upper canyon floor depth.
steps.quote: Their higher w/t suggest that these are more likely formed by laterally erosive river flows and are incised valleys, rather than canyons.

steps.action: Linked PV1–PV3 to published sea-level falls, palaeoclimate and catchment capture, and compared the estimated w/t of the onshore Kings Park Formation valley with PV1, proposing it as PV1's up-dip continuation.
steps.quote: We suggest that the 530–600 m deep Kings Park Formation palaeovalley is likely the up-dip continuation of the 400 m deep PV1 incised valley

steps.action: Inferred a long-term sedimentation rate of about 5 cm/ky from a published Bunbury Canyon core, by taking an organic, high-susceptibility horizon as the Last Glacial Maximum.
steps.quote: On this basis, a sedimentation rate of 5 cm/ky is inferred.

steps.action: Weighed the shelf-resuspension and slope-instability trigger against the earthquake differencing result, and judged the largest recorded earthquakes insufficient to cause widespread headwall failure.
steps.quote: have been insufficient to initiate widespread headwall failure

steps.action: Weighed the mass-movement trigger (scars with few blocks retained, implying hydroplaning runout) and the fan morphology (entrenched, lagged cyclic steps), concluding the fan is starved of sediment.
steps.quote: the proximal fan appears to be primarily starved of sediment

steps.action: Kept the claim that Perth Canyon was initiated in the Late Cretaceous by palaeo-Swan River incision (PV1), with decreasing activity through PV2–PV3, and that the modern canyon is relatively quiescent.
steps.quote: Perth Canyon first incised in the Late Cretaceous, when a pronounced relative sea level fall and wetter conditions in the catchment area

tree.answer: Shelf-incising Perth Canyon with mass-failure, incisional and aggradational features
Morphology yes (bathymetry); origin and history only through seismic and sediment traces
Map the geomorphology, determine geological controls, interpret evolution and recent activity
Yes: mass wasting versus turbidity currents; three turbidity triggers; cyclic steps versus failed blocks
Partly: w/t ratios separate incised valleys from canyons; internal structure and core separate cyclic steps from blocks
Found, not set: legacy seismic traces and a live 2018 earthquake sequence

tree.question: 6b
tree.answer: Partly: three successive stacked incised valleys and repeated cyclic-step fields
Limited: backscatter cross-checked against sub-bottom and samples; no sensitivity test of mapping thresholds
Best explanation: relict canyon initiated by a Late Cretaceous palaeo-Swan incised valley

end.claim: Perth Canyon first incised in the Late Cretaceous, when a sea-level fall and a wetter catchment cut a large palaeo-Swan River incised valley (PV1) that fed turbidity currents; activity declined through later incisions (PV2, PV3), and the modern canyon is relatively quiescent.

decisive_move.sentence: Identifying the three stacked palaeovalleys PV1–PV3 in legacy seismic landward of the headwall gave the age, scale and fluvial link on which the genesis claim rests.

gates.evidence: Action: the data were compiled from earlier surveys and legacy hydrocarbon seismic; only the 2018 repeat survey was aimed at a question (earthquake impact), and it did not bear on the genesis claim. Claim: the palaeovalley w/t ratios, the depth match with the canyon floor, and the Kings Park Formation comparison could have failed, but no decisive test discriminates the rivals, and the cyclic step versus block question is left open. Registration: TPI thresholds were chosen by trial and error after inspecting the data; nothing was fixed in advance.

novelty_claims.quote: features that for the first time provide detailed insights into the canyon's formative processes
to objectively map the complexity of the system in unprecedented detail
provide new insights into the likely timing of the Perth Canyon's initiation and periods of reactivation

limits:
The supplied XML text holds only the abstract and the figure and table captions, so body steps cite printed pages and quotes are copied from the PDF text. No review file was supplied, so no review sequence is coded; the acknowledgements say two anonymous reviewers improved the manuscript, but what they changed is not shown.

The TPI thresholds were selected by trial and error, and neither the values tried nor their effect on the map is reported. The geomorphic map extrapolates interpretations from a few representative units; how far mapped classes would change under other interpretations is not reported.

Sub-claims and their statuses:
- Structural control of the canyon course and of mass failures: best_explanation.
- Mid-canyon and mouth undulations as cyclic steps: best_explanation, with the failed-block alternative kept open. Deep cores are said to be needed, and a single core supports the mouth interpretation.
- Limited headwall change after the 2018 earthquakes: best_explanation. The 4-year differencing window prevents attribution to the earthquakes, and no grid uncertainty or detection threshold is given.
- Long-term sedimentation rate of about 5 cm/ky: an estimate from one published core with an assumed LGM horizon, without stated uncertainty.

Palaeovalley ages rest on vintage seismic of sub-optimal quality and a single representative line. Inference: two authors (Nanson, Post) co-authored the Dove et al. (2020) scheme applied here, so the method is partly the authors' own earlier work.

disagreements.target: Huang et al. (2014): Australian canyons reflect the dominance of mass wasting over shelf-initiated turbidity currents
disagreements.support: The paper argues that Perth Canyon's preferential extension needs further mechanisms, and attributes its initiation to fluvially fed turbidity currents through the palaeo-Swan incised valleys.
disagreements.quote: The preferential extension and enlargement of Perth Canyon invoke additional mechanisms for its formation

disagreements.target: Mitchell (2006); Micallef et al. (2014): fault-forced nick-points develop rounded, diffused profiles
disagreements.support: The long profiles show asymmetric nick-points, rounded upstream and angular downstream, which the authors ascribe to resistant strata or faulting in a high-energy constriction.
disagreements.quote: All three nick-points in the Perth Canyon mid-reach are asymmetrical, however, with more rounded upper-lip profiles that become more angular downstream

disagreements.target: Normark and Carlson (2003): low preservation of submarine fans explained by subduction on active margins
disagreements.support: For the passive-margin Perth fan, the entrenched fan valley and the gravel lag over cyclic steps point instead to reworking by erosive turbidity currents.
disagreements.quote: In the case of the Perth Canyon, however, the entrenched valley that dissects the fan

alternatives_considered.alternatives: Other threshold values tried by trial and error (not named)
alternatives_considered.reason: Trial and error; neighbourhood deemed large enough from visual inspection

alternatives_considered.alternatives: 40 m compilation grid for the lower reaches; 250 m regional grid outside the park
alternatives_considered.reason: Coverage: the 20 m grid represents most of the canyon

alternatives_considered.reason: Arcuate planform, downstream-reducing crest heights, hydraulic position in an expanding reach

alternatives_considered.chosen: Canyon-mouth Holes and Ridges as cyclic steps

alternatives_considered.reason: Hydraulic setting, upslope-dipping internal structure, turbidite packages in the core

alternatives_considered.reason: Incised-valley depth, w/t and timing tie PV1 to canyon initiation; low modern sedimentation and limited earthquake-driven failure
